newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns Syria on bomb charges.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns Syria on bomb charges.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it could not confirm a Syrian report that Israeli agents planted a bomb that killed nine people on a bus in Damascus and warned Syria against making "wild and irresponsible" statements without evidence.

"There have been over many many months a series of unexplained bombings and explosions in Damascus. The United States government has no information about these explosions and we certainly cannot confirm some of the rather wild reports coming out of Damascus this morning about who may have committeed these bombing attacks," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"It is a very serious charge for one state to accuse another of actually sponsoring bombings in its capital," Burns said, adding that it did not enhance the atmosphere for peacemaking.

"If the Syrian government and the Syrian press cannot back up what they are saying, well they ought not to make that charge. It's a wild and irresponsible charge if in fact it is not backed up by evidence," he said.
Syria said on Thursday that Israeli agents planted a bomb on a bus in central Damascus on Tuesday, killing nine people and wounding 44. Israel denied the charge.
"Nine people were killed and 44 others were wounded in the criminal action against a transport bus in Damascus," an official spokesman told the official Syrian news agency SANA.
"This terrorist, cowardly and criminal action comes within the framework of threats which were launched recently by Israeli officials that aim at killing the (Middle East) peace process," he said.

"Agents of the (Israeli intelligence agency) Mossad utilised preparations for the New Year celebrations on Tuesday 31.12.1996 with people leaving to their towns and planted an explosive device inside the bus which exploded minutes after it left the bus station at noon," the official said.
